incidents.title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition
incidents.title_en: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition
incidents.summary:
Angela Lipps, 50, of Tennessee is suing Fargo, North Dakota and police detective Lucas Heck for $10 million after being falsely arrested and jailed for about six months. She was taken at gunpoint from her home in July 2025 while babysitting four children, held nearly four months in a Tennessee jail awaiting extradition, then about two more months in North Dakota on theft and identity fraud charges. The charges were dropped after her lawyer supplied bank records showing she was in Tennessee when the Fargo fraud occurred, and she was released on Christmas Eve.

The lawsuit says a West Fargo investigator used AI facial recognition on a fake ID from surveillance video, and it returned Lipps's social media photo as a possible match. Detective Heck allegedly relied on that lead without further investigation or probable cause. Lipps says she lost her home, car, and belongings, was denied medications and dentures, and suffered lasting trauma. Fargo officials declined to comment on the pending litigation.

incidents.title_en: Former Costa Mesa Police Officer Pleads Guilty to Contacting His Mistress Thousands of Times Through Text, Phone Calls, and Social Media Messages, Including More than 100 Times in a Day, Illegally Accessing Confidential Law Enforcement Databases to Track Romantic Rivals, Ex-girlfriend, and Wife
incidents.summary:
A former Costa Mesa police officer pleaded guilty to contacting his mistress thousands of times through text messages, phone calls, and social media. On at least one occasion, he contacted her more than 100 times in a single day. He also admitted to illegally accessing confidential law enforcement databases to track his wife, an ex-girlfriend, and men he considered romantic rivals.

The case involves a former member of the Costa Mesa Police Department who misused his access to sensitive police systems. His guilty plea covers both the obsessive communications and the unauthorized database searches, which invaded the privacy of several people connected to his personal life. The available information does not specify a sentencing date or the exact penalties he faces.

incidents.title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal
incidents.title_en: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal
incidents.summary:
Two sisters from Rio Arriba County are suing the city of Española after a July 23 traffic stop. Jaclynn Gonzales, 21, was driving with her 12-year-old sister when a Flock Safety camera misread their license plate, confusing a final 2 for a 7 and flagging the car as stolen from Rio Rancho. Police stopped them on Calle Duran, handcuffed both, and placed them in separate patrol cars before realizing the error. Jaclynn asked officers to call their mother, who lived nearby, but the girl was still handcuffed and detained.

The lawsuits, filed January 3 in state District Court, seek unspecified damages for anxiety, fear, worry, and restricted movement. Their attorney, Sheri Raphaelson, also represents Adam Pacheco, who was 17 when he was wrongly stopped in a similar camera-related mistake in April. The city, police chief, and Flock Safety did not respond to requests for comment. The cases will now proceed in court.

incidents.title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated
incidents.title_en: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated
incidents.summary:
Rebecca Green agreed to let an AI scribe transcribe her first urologist appointment, but the tool invented a claim that she microdosed psychedelic mushrooms. She found the false statement in a post-operative letter sent to her GP after kidney stone surgery in March. Ms Green, who was receiving workers' compensation, feared the error could harm her case. After she complained, the urologist apologised, corrected the record, and said she would review how AI was used in her practice.

A Digital Rights Watch report found similar mistakes, including recording the wrong breast in a cancer diagnosis and inventing epilepsy. The Royal Australian College of GPs estimates 40 per cent of GPs regularly use AI scribes, though none are approved by the Therapeutic Goods Administration. The TGA has been reviewing these tools and will release findings in coming weeks, with breaches to be acted upon. The advocacy group wants the AI Safety Institute to test scribes and publish approved tools.

incidents.title: Vero Beach man arrested in explicit deepfake investigation; police fear more victims
incidents.title_en: Vero Beach man arrested in explicit deepfake investigation; police fear more victims
incidents.summary:
A 37-year-old Vero Beach man, Peter Solomon Ruma, was arrested after police say he used photos from social media and other online sources to create and share AI-generated sexually explicit images of women without their consent. Investigators searched his home and electronic devices on Wednesday and found evidence linking him to the images. Ruma is being held on a $1 million bond and faces eight charges tied to one female victim between June and August 2026, including three counts of creating altered sexual depictions, three counts of promoting them, one count of sexual cyber harassment, and one count of stalking.

Police have identified several additional possible victims who may not know images of them were made or shared, and they believe Ruma may have done this for years. The investigation is ongoing and more charges could be filed. Authorities are asking anyone who believes they were victimized or has information about the altered images to contact the Vero Beach Police Department.

incidents.title: L'homme qui a attaqué une garderie suisse a trouvé ses victimes sur ChatGPT
incidents.title_en: The man who attacked a Swiss daycare found his victims on ChatGPT
incidents.summary:
A 23-year-old Chinese student is on trial in Zurich for attempted murder after stabbing three five-year-old boys at a childcare center in Oerlikon on 1 October 2024. One boy had a major vein in his neck completely cut and needed emergency surgery, another suffered two chest wounds that damaged his heart and arteries and nearly died, and the third was injured in his ear and lung. A daycare worker grabbed the attacker's arms, forcing him to drop the knife and surrender before passersby held him for police.

Prosecutors say he planned the attack for weeks, using ChatGPT to ask about legal consequences of stabbing random victims, choosing children, ordering knives and clothing, studying anatomy, and buying raw beef to practice stabbing the day before. He acted on China's national day and posted patriotic and insulting messages just before the attack. The prosecution calls the crime exceptionally cold-blooded and is seeking a 15-year prison sentence and a 15-year expulsion order. The court hearing began Thursday.

incidents.title: Masked AI call forces Parkview High into soft lockdown
incidents.title_en: Masked AI call forces Parkview High into soft lockdown
incidents.summary:
Parkview High School in Gwinnett County, Georgia received its fourth AI-generated bomb threat of the school year so far on Monday. The school was placed on lockdown out of an abundance of caution before it eventually returned to normal operations. The latest threat used a masked phone number, the same pattern seen in recent incidents at the school.

In a letter to parents, school police said the incident followed a pattern involving masked phone numbers. Gwinnett County Public Schools police are working with the Georgia Bureau of Investigation and the FBI to determine who is responsible. Authorities have not announced any arrests or identified a suspect in connection with the threats, according to Gwinnett Schools Police. The investigation is ongoing.

stories.Headline: Sen. Bernie Sanders unveils bill to ban artificial superintelligence and create Department of AI
stories.Summary:
Senator Bernie Sanders and Representative Greg Casar introduced legislation Wednesday to permanently ban artificial superintelligence, meaning systems that exceed human cognitive ability or could plan humanity's destruction. The bill would pause development of the most advanced AI until a new Department of Artificial Intelligence sets federal safety rules, and such systems would then need federal approval before use. Violations could lead to penalties including up to 20 years in prison. Some employees at OpenAI and Google DeepMind supported the measure.

The bill faces long odds in the Republican-controlled Congress, where even less sweeping AI rules have stalled. President Donald Trump has opposed oversight and recently told the United Nations he would rename AI super intelligence. Sanders said avoiding dangerous AI will require cooperation with China, like nuclear arms control during the Cold War. The proposal is unlikely to pass but shows how progressive Democrats plan to raise AI regulation in upcoming elections.

stories.Headline: Trump to rename AI into SI 'Super Intelligence'
stories.Summary:
President Donald Trump announced at the United Nations General Assembly on September 22, 2026 that he is ordering the term “Artificial Intelligence” to be replaced with “Super Intelligence,” or SI, in all official U.S. documents. He told world leaders that the word “artificial” makes the technology sound fake, when he believes it is actually amazing, and that “super” is more accurate. He also rejected any global plan to regulate AI, saying the United States must not fall behind China in an AI arms race.

The article notes that “super intelligence” already exists as an industry term for AI that surpasses human intelligence, and it is both a goal for many companies and a concern for critics. Trump said that from now on, U.S. documents, and hopefully those of other countries, will use the new name. No further steps or timeline were given beyond this announcement.

stories.Headline: Vyzoxa Redefines AI Learning Through Practical AI Agent Development, Empowering Learners Worldwide to Build With Artificial Intelligence
stories.Summary:
Vyzoxa, an education technology platform run by NDFM Business World Pvt. Ltd., has introduced a practical artificial intelligence learning pathway. It aims to help one million people become AI innovators by 2030. Participants first complete about two weeks of AI agent industrial training with recorded lessons and daily tasks. They then move into a four week project based internship in AI agent development at no extra cost, where they build and present a working AI agent. The program is remote and self paced, open to learners in India and many international regions.

The platform includes AI tools called Vyzoxa Intelligent Systems, such as an AI mentor, AI coder, and AI engine, to support learning and project work. Founder Mansajan Singh and Managing Director Gurjinder Singh lead the company. For eligible participants in India, top performers may be shortlisted for a final interview and could receive employment or pre-placement offers, but these are performance based and not guaranteed. The article does not state a specific next step beyond the platform's ongoing mission and enrollment.

stories.Headline: Pritzker signs executive order establishing Illinois Artificial Intelligence Cabinet - metropolisplanet.com
stories.Summary:
Governor JB Pritzker signed an executive order on Tuesday creating the Illinois Artificial Intelligence Cabinet. The group will assess risks that artificial intelligence could pose to the safety of Illinois residents and advise state agencies on preparing for and responding to AI related incidents. It will also recommend safeguards for public buildings, water systems, education systems, and information infrastructure. Members will include experts from academia, law, ethics, and governance, plus leaders from eight state agencies including the Illinois State Police and the Department of Public Health.

The cabinet follows the Artificial Intelligence Safety Measures Act that Pritzker signed in July, and his office said it responds to a lack of federal action and a whistleblower's resignation in the AI industry. In the coming weeks, Pritzker will announce appointed members. The cabinet will evaluate state rules, tying data center tax incentives to safety standards, addressing energy burdens from AI data centers, adding AI safety standards to state contracts, and considering strict liability for AI caused harm. Lt. Gov. Juliana Stratton said Illinois is prioritizing the issue to protect people.

stories.Headline: Banks Warn AI Shopping Bots Raise Scam, Fraud and Data-Privacy Risks
stories.Summary:
A group of banks, including NatWest, Bank of America, ING, Capital One, ASB Bank, and Commonwealth Bank of Australia, warned on September 22 that AI shopping agents could increase scams, fraud, and data privacy breaches. They noted that technology firms like OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Meta are promoting chatbots to select products and buy on behalf of shoppers. British retailer John Lewis said AI agent searches grew to 2.5 percent from 0.3 percent a year earlier. The banks said customers are interested but the technology is moving faster than consumer protections.

The report highlighted risks such as AI agents taking card details and entering them directly into websites, or pushing users toward payment methods with weaker safeguards. Consumers worry about wrong purchases, overspending, or losing money to fraud, and are unsure who would help. The banks plan to discuss proposals with policymakers, including requiring disclosure when an AI agent is involved, more transparency about how agents decide, safeguards for customer data, and allowing consumers and merchants to choose interoperable AI shopping services.

stories.Headline: Pritzker establishes AI cabinet amid calls for greater regulation
stories.Summary:
Illinois Governor JB Pritzker signed an executive order on Tuesday creating an artificial intelligence cabinet made up of unpaid experts and state agency representatives. The group will develop policy proposals through 2027 and examine risks AI poses to residents and critical infrastructure such as water systems, education, and information networks. It will also study emerging AI incidents and recommend safety, accountability, and transparency measures, including possible conditions on data center incentives and reviews of energy grid strain.

The move follows a whistleblower's claim that AI could become uncontrollable by 2030, and it builds on Illinois' Artificial Intelligence Safety Measures Act signed in July. That law targets AI models earning over $500 million annually, requires reporting on risks like weapons creation or cyberattacks, and mandates annual audits starting in 2028. Pritzker is urging Congress to hold hearings and set national standards, saying AI is as dangerous as nuclear weapons and needs international cooperation.

stories.Headline: Privacy Commissioner puts Manage My Health, Health NZ on notice after data breach
stories.Summary:
The Privacy Commissioner has issued formal compliance notices to Health New Zealand and the patient portal Manage My Health after a December 2025 cyber attack on the portal. Hackers leaked data belonging to almost 100,000 people, about 90 percent of them in Northland. The stolen files included 403,730 Health New Zealand documents and 22,609 documents uploaded by patients. An earlier investigation found both organisations failed to have adequate security controls under the Health Information Privacy Code.

Commissioner Michael Webster said the notices require the two bodies to meet security obligations and give patients confidence their data is being protected. Manage My Health has already improved multifactor authentication and restricted unauthorised access. It must complete all required changes by the end of August 2027, while Health New Zealand has until the end of January. Webster noted the impact on Māori in Northland, where most affected patients live.

stories.Headline: Virginia governor presses Congress for AI guardrails
stories.Summary:
Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger sent a letter to top congressional leaders, including House Speaker Mike Johnson and Senate Majority Leader John Thune, urging them to set national rules for artificial intelligence. She warned that leaving oversight mainly to private companies could threaten jobs, privacy, and public resources. Spanberger also announced state-level steps, such as a data center accountability framework and an executive order creating an AI task force, but she did not propose specific federal legislation or give a timetable for recommendations.

A recent Reuters/Ipsos poll found that 73 percent of Americans believe AI companies have not done enough to prevent serious harm, while 55 percent support slowing AI development and 13 percent oppose it. Last year, the Senate voted 99 to 1 to remove a provision that would have discouraged states from regulating AI. Representative Don Beyer and ten other House members also pressed for federal action. Congress remains divided, and Johnson has said he will not rush to regulate, so no immediate federal legislation is certain.

stories.Headline: Onco-Innovations and Redwood AI Secure Terry Fox Research Institute Grant to Advance AI-Powered SynoGraph(TM) Oncology Platform
stories.Summary:
Onco-Innovations, as lead applicant, and Redwood AI, along with Canada's Michael Smith Genome Sciences Centre and Centre de recherche du CHU de Québec-Université Laval, have received a grant from the Terry Fox Research Institute's Digital Health Innovation Fund. The funding supports development of SynoGraph, an AI platform that uses causal AI and federated learning to predict first-in-human clinical outcomes from preclinical and real-world patient data. The grant is reimbursement based, covering up to 25 percent of an estimated $3.5 million project budget.

Under the contribution agreements, Redwood AI will provide data integration and physicochemical modelling methods, while the two research centres will supply clinico-genomic and imaging data to enable federated learning while protecting privacy. The project aims to improve prediction of clinical outcomes and support therapy development. The article does not specify a next milestone beyond the collaborative work proceeding under these agreements.
